title: Automated evidence bundles and proactive PagerDuty briefs for latency/error incidents
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: Build a safe, size-conscious evidence-bundling service that attaches compact telemetry snapshots and actionable runbook snippets to PagerDuty alerts and Slack incidents. The bundle should contain: compact span excerpts, top-3 related traces, a short error/latency summary, relevant SLO context, and a canonical runbook extract with one-click remediation actions. We will prefer signed links to a short-lived artifact store for large payloads and inline context for immediate triage. The service must respect PII/sensitive-data redaction rules and rate-limit attachments during noisy events.
acceptance_criteria: PD alerts for severity P1-P0 include a link to an evidence bundle and a 3-line summary in the PD description
Slack incident threads created by alerts include an attachable playbook card with deep links to runbook steps
Evidence bundle size capped at 500KB for inline payloads; larger artifacts stored in signed S3 blobs with access tokens that expire in 1 hour
Automatic PII redaction applied to traces and logs before bundle creation; redaction rules verified by security team
End-to-end latency to generate and attach a brief must be <5s for sampled incidents and <30s for full bundles
Feature toggles exist per-customer and per-route to disable attachment/linking
tasks: Design proto schema for evidence bundle (compact trace extract, metadata, runbook snippet, SLO snapshot)
Implement evidence-bundler microservice (ingest hooks from tracing and logs pipelines)
Add PD integration: attach summary + link and PD quick actions (runbook-run, rollback) via PD API
Add Slack integration: post incident cards with interactive buttons that surface runbook steps
Implement sampling policy and burst suppression to avoid alert storms
Add PII redaction pipeline and security audit checklist
Create end-to-end tests and a Playground dashboard for QA team
Documentation: runbook template guide + admin toggle guide
decisions: Will use signed short-lived blob links for large payloads instead of uploading full attachments to PagerDuty due to PD size limits and rate limits
Evidence bundler will be a new standalone microservice in the observability namespace to keep runtime isolation and auth boundaries clear
Sampling policy: deterministic sampling for high-traffic endpoints (1% baseline) with immediate sampling for SLA breaches
Runbook snippets will be authored as markdown fragments stored in our runbook repo; UI will render first 3 steps inline and link to full document
implementation_notes: Bundle schema v1: {summary, top_traces[], top_spans[], slo_snapshot, runbook_ref, metadata}
Trace extraction: use trace-collector to extract contiguous span windows around error span ID +/- 200ms; limit to 10 spans per trace
Store bundles in S3-compatible store with KMS-encrypted objects and signed URL generation service
PD integration uses Events V2 API for alert enrichment and the Notes field for the 3-line summary; Quick Actions implemented via PD action links to our operator console
Slack cards use Block Kit with action buttons wired to our ops-run API; authentication via OIDC tokens scoped to the incident channel
Redaction: run logs through scrubbing rules (regex + schema inference). Any bundle failing redact validation is blocked from publishing and marked for manual review
Telemetry: emit metrics for bundles_created, bundle_size_bytes, attach_latency_seconds, attach_failures_total
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): internal infra team only; attach links to PD but not Slack; monitor attach_latency and attach_failures for 72h
Phase 1: opt-in early customers + ops channels; expose runbook snippets for a subset of incident types
Phase 2: default-on for P1/P0 routes, Slack cards enabled; enable automatic sampling policies
Rollback: toggle to disable attachments globally and revert to baseline PD alerts
Post-rollout: runbook authoring blitz to populate top 20 operational runbooks
